error_magnitude_caveat: 1 m is the accuracy of individual LOLA measurements, NOT of the gridded 237 m LDEM_128: it leaves out gridding/interpolation error between ground tracks, which Barker et al. 2023 (PSJ 4, 183, Sec. 3) show dominates gridded-DEM height error and grows with effective resolution. No published figure for LDEM_128's gridded error was found. For scale, the merged SLDEM2015 has a stated typical vertical accuracy of 3-4 m (Barker et al. 2016) -- a different product. See sensitivity_assumed_error for sigma at a larger assumed error.
error_model_basis: No per-pixel error raster is published for LDEM_128 (PDS LOLA GDR cylindrical/img + float_img contain only .img/.lbl/.xml; PGDA products 78 and 90 cover only 60S-pole; SLDEM2015, PGDA product 54, publishes none either). The DEM was therefore perturbed by a CONSTANT 1-sigma elevation error of 1 m: LOLA's ~1 m absolute vertical accuracy from orbit-overlap analysis (Mazarico et al. 2013, as cited by Barker et al. 2016, Icarus 273, 346-355). The error is assumed Gaussian, 1-sigma, uniform over the window.
notes: PRELIMINARY ASSUMED-ERROR Monte-Carlo: constant 1 m 1-sigma DEM error (no error raster exists for LDEM_128); not a measured uncertainty.

perturbation_model.construction: white noise smoothed by a Gaussian kernel, renormalized to unit variance, scaled by the constant assumed error
perturbation_model.note: The correlation length (50 m) is below the 237 m pixel size, so the field is effectively uncorrelated between pixels.

status: PRELIMINARY -- ASSUMED-ERROR sigma, not a measured uncertainty; see error_model

validation_status.note: Re-running the production mask generator on the current DEM window reproduces this nominal exactly, but not the published mask bit for bit (difference above). Sigma is a spread, so this small nominal offset is not expected to matter; the published mask was not regenerated.

vertical_datum_caveat: The vertical datum of LDEM_128 relative to the 1,737,400 m sphere follows its PDS label (OFFSET=1737400); sigma is a spread statistic and is unaffected by a constant offset.
